speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin my assessment, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) with Pancoast Syndrome.

The combination of progressive arm weakness, decreased sensation, significant weight loss, and your history of smoking and diabetes strongly suggests an upper thoracic malignancy invading the sympathetic chain and brachial plexus. I need to confirm this with imaging; REQUEST IMAGES: Chest CT with contrast. Additionally, given your age and symptoms, we must rule out metabolic causes; REQUEST TEST: HbA1c and TSH.
